name: SK Hynix
day_summary: SK Hynix rose +1.8% to ₩268,000 — green on a red day. While the KOSPI fell ~0.9% on the global risk-off and a weak won, the HBM memory leader was bought as the cleanest Asian beneficiary of the AI capital rotation. Longs and the foreign bid won; this was the relative-strength leader of the whole market.
long_pnl: +1.8% — longs paid, outperformed a red KOSPI

decision.rationale: SK Hynix is the supply-side twin of the long-AI trade: the lead supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to Nvidia, with demand that is inelastic to the week's macro. It is showing genuine relative strength — green while the KOSPI and global risk are red — because the AI rotation that is draining crypto flows straight into HBM. BUY at medium conviction, but mind two Korea-specific risks: a won sliding toward 1,400/USD eats foreign-currency returns, and the stock is the index's single biggest swing factor, so it falls hard if HBM pricing or Nvidia capex ever blinks. Own the leader; scale adds on macro-driven dips toward ₩250,000.

positioning.notable_flow: Foreign institutions were net buyers of SK Hynix even as they sold the broad KOSPI — a clear rotation into the AI-memory leader. The risk cuts both ways: with foreigners owning ~54% of the float, a won break above 1,400/USD can trigger FX-driven selling regardless of the HBM story.

what_traders_are_doing: Desks are treating SK Hynix as the Asian leg of the global 'long AI infrastructure' trade — the memory bottleneck that Nvidia's accelerators can't run without. It is the relative-strength leader of the KOSPI, bought on dips by foreign institutions, while won-sensitive and cyclical names are sold. The crowd is long the HBM cycle; the hedge most traders watch is USD/KRW, not the stock itself.

analysis:
## The two sides of one trade

The cleanest way to understand SK Hynix in 2026 is as the **supply side of the same trade that NVIDIA is the demand side of**. Nvidia sells the accelerators; SK Hynix makes the [high-bandwidth memory those accelerators cannot run without](https://en.yna.co.kr/). So when capital rotates out of crypto and speculative risk and into AI, it doesn't just buy Nvidia — it buys the memory bottleneck, and SK Hynix is the technology leader there.

## Why it's green on a red day

On June 8 the KOSPI fell ~0.9% on a weak won and the global risk-off, yet SK Hynix rose +1.8%. That divergence is the whole thesis: [foreign institutions sold the broad index but bought the AI-memory leader](https://www.koreaherald.com/). HBM demand is inelastic to the week's macro, and supply for the Blackwell/Rubin ramp is tight.

## The catch: the won

SK Hynix is **~54% foreign-owned**, which makes it as much an FX instrument as a semiconductor one. With [USD/KRW grinding toward 1,400](https://www.koreaherald.com/), an unhedged dollar investor is also short the won — and a decisive break of 1,400 can trigger foreign selling that overwhelms the HBM bid. That is why the BUY is medium-conviction and scaled, and why the level most traders watch is the currency, not the chart.

## What would change the call

A hot [May CPI on June 10](https://www.investing.com/indices/kospi) that drives the won through 1,400 turns this into a HOLD until the FX stabilizes — the HBM thesis stays intact, but the tape would tell you FX is in control. A cool CPI with the won holding below 1,400 reopens a run at the ₩285,000 high.
